title: Extending a normalized resolution rule by an initial conductor blowup
statement:
Let $N$ assign to every normal reduced finite-type $\mathbf Q$-scheme $S$, including finite disjoint unions, a finite tower of normalized blowups [def-trf-normalized-blowup] starting at $S$, with coherent ideals whose zero schemes are nonempty and nowhere dense and with regular terminal scheme [def-weil-regular-scheme]. Normal means that the local rings are integrally closed domains [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Suppose that $N$ has canonical comparisons for every smooth morphism of such schemes [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]: the tower on the source is the recursively pulled-back tower on the target with exactly its unit-ideal stages deleted, retaining the other extended ideals in order. Assume these comparisons respect identities and composition, and delete no stage for a surjective morphism. Assume $N(\varnothing)$ is trivial.

For any reduced finite-type $\mathbf Q$-scheme $X$ [def-pc-reduced-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], let $\nu:X^\nu\to X$ be componentwise normalization [def-weil-pbc-reduced-normalization] and set
$$D_X=\operatorname{Ann}_{\mathcal O_X}\operatorname{coker}(\mathcal O_X\longrightarrow\nu_*\mathcal O_{X^\nu}),\qquad P(X)=\operatorname{Bl}_{D_X}(X)^\nu.$$
Here the cokernel is [def-trf-conductor-cokernel], and annihilator consists of local functions killing all local sections. Define $H_N(X)$ to be $P(X)\to X$ followed by $N(P(X))$, omitting the first stage exactly when $D_X=\mathcal O_X$. Then $D_X$ is coherent with nowhere dense zero scheme, $D_X=\mathcal O_X$ exactly when $X$ is normal, and $P(X)$ is normal, reduced and of finite type. This formula defines a finite normalized blowup tower for every $X$, with nonempty nowhere dense centers and regular terminal scheme, and $H_N(\varnothing)$ is trivial.

For every smooth $h:Y\to X$ between reduced finite-type $\mathbf Q$-schemes, $D_Y=D_X\mathcal O_Y$ and $P(Y)\simeq P(X)\times_XY$ canonically, with smooth induced map to $P(X)$. The resulting comparisons identify $H_N(Y)$ with $(h^*H_N(X))^c$, preserving ordered extended ideals and respecting identities and composition; a unit-ideal stage is omitted only when its normalized blowup is an isomorphism. If $h$ is surjective, no stage is contracted.

proof.text: Use the conductor geometry and smooth preparation square, whose unchanged proofs and concrete input definitions are now in the preparation module. They are derived from the same conductor and normalized-blowup calculus as before.

Define T(X) as the explicit conductor extension of N(P(X)). Its normalized resolution fields and exact extension specification are given by the tower construction. Choose the smooth comparisons from their characterization unique on all downstream index and map data.

Construct the identity comparison explicitly with unchanged tower, identity maps and identity contraction. The uniqueness clauses of the conductor comparison give both identity laws. Apply the generic comparison laws to fill composition and surjectivity fields of the smooth rule. On an empty X, stalkwise normality is vacuous, so the conductor is unit. P(X) is empty because it maps to X. N.empty gives its tail length zero, and the unit construction preserves length. Assemble the rule with the pointwise exact extension witness.

Steps 2 and 4: the conductor node gives a coherent, nowhere-dense D that is unit exactly when X is normal, and D_Y = D_X O_Y. These meet the hypotheses of the normalized-blowup calculus, which gives P(X) normal, reduced and of finite type, B_O(S) = S for normal S, and P(Y) ≅ P(X) ×_X Y with h̄ smooth. Step 5: the conductor stage is deleted only when D_Y is unit; then Y is normal and that stage is an isomorphism. Step 6: the induction has an explicit base and step, and every deleted source level is normal. Step 7: composition and identities follow from the cited statements' compatibility clauses, and the retained-index argument is written out. Step 8: the local stalk map keeps D_Y proper above V(D_X), and surjective base change makes h̄ surjective, which matches ILO 2.3.5(i). I tested: the empty scheme, a normal X, the cusp, the inclusion of the normal locus, a surjective double cover, and a nonunit center whose normalized blowup is an isomorphism.
